h: Joseph Becomes the Channel of Blessing

p: וּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים שֶׁהֵם כְּלַל צוֹרְכֵי הָאָדָם, חַיֵּי בְּנֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי, וּבִשְׁלָשְׁתָּן כְּתִיב בְּרָכָה.
— Three things encompass human needs—life, children, and sustenance—and blessing is mentioned regarding all three.
בְּנֵי, בְּרָכָה דְּאָדָם פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ.
— Children: the blessing given to Adam, “Be fruitful and multiply.”
מְזוֹנֵי, כְּתִיב בִּרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר.
— Sustenance: it is written, “The blessing of Hashem brings wealth.”
חַיֵּי, כְּתִיב וּבֵרַךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ וְאֶת מֵימֶיךָ וַהֲסִירוֹתִי מַחֲלָה מִקִּרְבֶּךָ.
— Life: it is written, “He shall bless your bread and your water, and I shall remove illness from your midst.”
וּשְׁלָשְׁתָּן הַהַשְׁפָּעָה מֵעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא, כִּדְאִיתָא (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כח.)
— The influx of all three comes from Atika Kadisha, as it is taught (Moed Katan 28a):
חַיֵּי בְּנֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי לָא בִּזְכוּתָא תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא אֶלָּא בְּמַזָּלָא תַּלְיָא.
— Life, children, and sustenance depend upon mazal rather than merit.
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג׳ עט ב) דְּמַזָּלָא קַדִּישָׁא הַיְינוּ עַתִּיקָא,
— The holy Zohar (III, 79b) teaches that the holy mazal is Atika,
וְהוּא מִדַּת אַיִן, וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קנו.) אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת אַיִן.
— which is the attribute of Ayin, Nothingness. Thus they say (Shabbat 156a), “There is no mazal for Israel”: Ayin itself is their source.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Resisei Layla 58:2: “For ‘children, life and sustenance do not depend on merit but on mazal’ (Moed Katan 28a). It is known that mazal is the root of the soul in its source, which drips and trickles vitality into all the extensions of the soul. And for ‘there is no mazal for Israel’ the explanation is known: Ayin, Nothingness, is their mazal. That is, the root of their vitality and the strength of their soul is that they are nothing and naught of themselves, except what Hashem bestows; and this is what drips and trickles to them the flow of children, life and sustenance. But from the side of their separation into selfhood, as though they were a separate something, they have no existence and no flow of children, life and sustenance at all. For they are not under the mazal of selfhood beneath the heavens, the rule of the stars and constellations, which is the mazal of the idolatrous nations, who receive a flow of children, life and sustenance of selfhood from the mazal beneath the heavens.”

h: Shabbat as the Source of Blessing

p: וּבְשַׁבָּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא, זְמַן הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לִשְׁלָשְׁתָּן,
— Shabbat, when Atika is revealed, is the time for the influx of all three.
דִּכְתִיב וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי, וְלֹא פֵירֵשׁ מַהוּ הַבְּרָכָה,
— For it says, “God blessed the seventh day,” without specifying the blessing.
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל מִינֵי בְרָכָה,
— It must therefore include every kind of blessing:
וְהֵם כָּל ג׳ דְּבָרִים שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהֶם בְּרָכָה, שֶׁהֵם כְּלַל הַבְּרָכוֹת.
— all three things regarding which blessing is written, encompassing all blessings.
וְשַׁבָּת בִּרְכָאן דְּכוֹלָּא בֵּיהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ דְּמִתְבָּרְכָאן מִינֵּיהּ כָּל שִׁיתָא יוֹמִין,
— Shabbat contains everyone’s blessings, as the holy Zohar says: all six days receive blessing from it.
שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹר הַבְּרָכָה, וְהַבְּרָכָה שֶׁלָּהֶם בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת.
— It is the source of blessing, and their blessing is on Shabbat.
וּבְפָרָשָׁה זוֹ וַיְבָרֲכֵם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא לֵאמוֹר בְּךָ יְבָרֵךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר.
— In this portion it says, “He blessed them on that day, saying: Through you Israel shall bless,” and so forth.
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רלג א) מְדַקְדֵּק מַאי בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא,
— The holy Zohar (233a) asks what “on that day” means.
דְּמַה שַּׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא כְּאִלּוּ כְּבָר בֵּרְכָם בְּיוֹם אַחֵר וְאוֹמֵר שֶׁבֵּרְכָם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא,
— Why say “on that day,” as though he had already blessed them on another day and now specifies that he blessed them on that day?
הֲלֹא עַכְשָׁיו בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם עוֹמֵד.
— Surely he is presently standing within that very day.
וְגַם מְדַקְדֵּק בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב לֵאמוֹר בְּוָיו, וּבְכָל מָקוֹם לֵאמֹר כְּתִיב חָסֵר.
— The holy Zohar also asks why leimor, “saying,” is spelled with a vav here, whereas elsewhere it is spelled defectively.
גַּם כָּל תֵּיבַת לֵאמֹר אֵין לוֹ פֵּירוּשׁ כָּאן,
— Moreover, the word “saying” itself has no apparent meaning here,
דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם לֵאמֹר, שֶׁצִּוָּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה לֵאמֹר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
— for elsewhere “saying” means that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded Moses to tell Israel.
וְכֵן בְּךָ יְבָרֵךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַמְבָרְכִים יֹאמְרוּ כֵן,
— Likewise “Through you Israel shall bless, saying” means that those giving blessings shall say this.
אֲבָל כָּאן שֶׁהַבְּרָכָה לָהֶם בְּעַצְמָם, הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר וַיְבָרֲכֵם וַיֹּאמַר,
— But here the blessing is addressed to them themselves, so it should say, “He blessed them and said,”
כְּדִלְעֵיל וַיְבָרֶךְ אֶת יוֹסֵף וַיֹּאמַר.
— as above, “He blessed Joseph and said.”
גַּם מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּךָ יְבָרֵךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל, דַּיְיקָא בְּךָ,
— Furthermore, why does “Through you Israel shall bless” specify “through you”?
וְלָמָּה יְבָרְכוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת עַצְמָם בְּיוֹסֵף דַּוְקָא,
— Why should all Israel invoke Joseph specifically in blessing themselves?
וַהֲלֹא מָצִינוּ בְּבִרְכַּת יְהוּדָה שֶׁמְּעוּלָּה מִבִּרְכַּת יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהֲרֵי עֲשָׂאוֹ מֶלֶךְ גַּם עָלָיו,
— Judah’s blessing appears superior to Joseph’s, for he was made king over Joseph as well,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר יִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ בְּנֵי אָבִיךָ וְגוֹמֵר,
— as it says, “Your father’s sons shall bow to you,” and so forth,
לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה וְגוֹמֵר עַד כִּי יָבֹא שִׁילֹה.
— “The scepter shall not depart from Judah,” and so forth, “until Shiloh comes.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 88a: ““Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: It is written, “God blessed the seventh day,” yet concerning manna it is written, “Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, Shabbat, there will be none.” Since no sustenance is found on that day, what blessing is found in it? Rather, we learned: All blessings above and below depend upon the seventh day. Why was no manna found on the seventh day? Because from that day all six supernal days receive blessing. Each gives its sustenance below, each on its own day, from the blessing with which they were blessed on the seventh day.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 233a: “Rabbi Yehudah opened and said: “He blessed them on that day, saying: Through you Israel will bless.” “He blessed them on that day”—what does “on that day” mean? It would have been enough to say “he blessed them.” Moreover, everywhere leimor is written defectively, but here it is written with a vav. Why the difference? Rather, it is a mystery. “He blessed them on that day”—this is the mystery of the degree appointed over blessings above. “That day”—a day from the supernal place called “He.” In “that day” there is no separation between “day” and “He”; wherever “that day” occurs, these are two degrees, an upper degree and a lower degree united as one. Therefore, when Jacob wished to bless Joseph’s sons, he blessed them through the union of above and below, all as one, so that their blessing would endure. Then he included everything together and said: “Through you Israel will bless.” What is “through you”? This is certainly the mystery of union: first from below upward, and afterward descending to the middle and below. Leimor with a vav is the middle; afterward it descends below, “through you.” This is properly ordered, from below upward and from above downward. “Through you Israel will bless”—who is Israel? Israel Sava. It does not say “Israel will be blessed,” but “will bless,” for Israel receives blessings from above and afterward blesses everything through precisely this lower degree, of which it says: “Through you Israel will bless, saying.””

: “Rabbi Yehudah opened and said: “He blessed them on that day, saying: Through you Israel will bless.” “He blessed them on that day”—what does “on that day” mean? It would have been enough to say “he blessed them.” Moreover, everywhere leimor is written defectively, but here it is written with a vav. Why the difference? Rather, it is a mystery. “He blessed them on that day”—this is the mystery of the degree appointed over blessings above. “That day”—a day from the supernal place called “He.” In “that day” there is no separation between “day” and “He”; wherever “that day” occurs, these are two degrees, an upper degree and a lower degree united as one. Therefore, when Jacob wished to bless Joseph’s sons, he blessed them through the union of above and below, all as one, so that their blessing would endure. Then he included everything together and said: “Through you Israel will bless.” What is “through you”? This is certainly the mystery of union: first from below upward, and afterward descending to the middle and below. Leimor with a vav is the middle; afterward it descends below, “through you.” This is properly ordered, from below upward and from above downward. “Through you Israel will bless”—who is Israel? Israel Sava. It does not say “Israel will be blessed,” but “will bless,” for Israel receives blessings from above and afterward blesses everything through precisely this lower degree, of which it says: “Through you Israel will bless, saying.””

h: Joseph Draws Blessing From Its Root

p: אָכֵן יֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז בָּזֶה שֶׁבֵּרַךְ אֶת יוֹסֵף,
— Rather, this may hint that he blessed Joseph
שֶׁהוּא דַּיְיקָא יִהְיֶה מְקוֹר הַבְּרָכוֹת וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשְׁפָּעַת הַבְּרָכוֹת כְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת.
— to become specifically the source of blessings and the root of their influx, like Shabbat.
שֶׁהַמְשָׁכַת הַשֶּׁפַע בְּרָכָה מֵהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא הוּא בְּג׳ מַדְרֵיגוֹת,
— The drawing of the flow of blessing from its root in Atika Kaddisha proceeds through three levels,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ, וְהַאי יוֹמָא מַלְיָא רֵישֵׁיהּ דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין מִטַּלָּא דְּנָחִית מֵעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא,
— as the holy Zohar teaches: on this day the head of Zeir Anpin is filled with dew descending from Atika Kadisha,
וְאַטִּיל לַחֲקְלָא דְּתַפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין, שֶׁנֶּגְדָּם הַג׳ סְעוּדוֹת.
— which it sends into the field of holy apples; the three meals correspond to these levels.
וּבְזֹהַר חָדָשׁ (פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא) מְבוֹאָר דְּיוֹסֵף הוּא בְּרָזָא דְּשַׁבָּת,
— Zohar Chadash, Ki Tissa, explains that Joseph belongs to the mystery of Shabbat,
כִּי שַׁבָּת הוּא בְּרָזָא דִּבְרִית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ צב רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳).
— for Shabbat belongs to the mystery of the covenant, as it says (Zohar II, 92a, beginning).
וְשָׁם (קלה ב), אֲפִיקוּ דְּבִרְכָאן מִמְּקוֹרָא דְּחַיֵּי וְכוּלֵי, בְּרָזָא דְּאָת קַייָּמָא וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּן שָׁם,
— And there (135b): the outflow of blessings from the source of life, and so forth, in the mystery of the sign of the covenant, and so forth; see there.
כִּי יוֹסֵף הוּא צִינּוֹר דְּהַמְשָׁכַת הַבְּרָכוֹת מִמָּקוֹר הָעֶלְיוֹן.
— For Joseph is the channel drawing blessings from the supernal source.
וְזֶה שֶׁבֵּרְכוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא, שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא,
— Thus he blessed him “on that day,” alluding to Atika Kadisha.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 88a: “Rabbi Abba said: Blessing is made ready for those supernal days, which are blessed from this day. This day fills the head of Zeir Anpin with the dew that descends from the Holy Ancient One, concealed beyond everything, and He casts it into the field of holy apples three times from the entrance of Shabbat, so that all will be blessed together. Therefore a person must take delight at these three times, for the faith above depends upon this: the Holy Ancient One, Zeir Anpin, and the field of apples. A person must delight in them and rejoice in them. Whoever omits one of these meals displays a defect above, and his punishment is great.”

p: שֶׁאֲנַחְנוּ מְכַנִּים אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה בְּחִינוֹת, הוּא אַתָּה אֲנִי.
— We refer to Hashem in three aspects: “He,” “You,” and “I.”
הוּא רוֹמֵז עַל עַתִּיקָא, שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן נִסְתָּר וְנֶעְלָם, שֵׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן.
— “He” alludes to Atika, using language of the concealed and hidden: the intellect concealed from every thought.
אַתָּה מְרַמֵּז עַל זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם הֲוָיָה,
— “You” alludes to Zeir Anpin, the Name Havayah,
שֶׁאָנוּ מְדַבְּרִים לְנוֹכַח אַתָּה הַשֵּׁם, כַּיָּדוּעַ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ רצ א).
— whom we address directly as “You, Hashem,” as is known (Zohar III, 290a).
אֲנִי מְרַמֵּז עַל הַשְּׁכִינָה, וְהִיא חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין, נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— “I” alludes to the Divine Presence, the field of apples, the souls of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אֲנִי הַשֵּׁם שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (שָׁם רכג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳).
— as it says, “I, Hashem, dwell among the children of Israel” (ibid., 223a, beginning).
וְהֵם הַג׳ שֵׁמוֹת אֶהְיֶ״ה הֲוָיָ״ה אֲדֹנָ״י,
— These are the three Names Ehyeh, Havayah, and Adonai.
דְּאֶהְיֶה רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ עַתָּה, רַק שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד, דְּאָז יִתְגַּלֶּה זֶה.
— Ehyeh, “I shall be,” signifies what is not presently manifest but will be in the future, when it will be revealed.
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא מְרַמֵּז לֶעָתִיד שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הַנֶּעְלָם.
— Everywhere “on that day” alludes to the future, when the concealed will be revealed.
וְכֵן כָּאן בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא מְרַמֵּז עַל עַתִּיקָא, שֵׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן,
— So here, “on that day” alludes to Atika, the intellect concealed from every thought:
וְהַיְינוּ טַלָּא דְּנָחִית מֵעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא.
— the dew descending from Atika Kadisha.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: שֶׁאָנוּ מְדַבְּרִים לְנוֹכַח אַתָּה הַשֵּׁם, כַּיָּדוּעַ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ רצ א)

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 290a, Idra Zuta: “This wisdom is called Eden, and this Eden is drawn from the supernal Eden, the most concealed of all concealed things. From this Eden a beginning is spoken of. In Atika there is no such designation, and there is neither beginning nor end. Because there is neither beginning nor end in it, it is not called “You,” for it is hidden and unrevealed; it is called “He.” From the place where a beginning is found, it is called “You” and “Father,” as it is written: “For You are our Father.” In the aggadah of the school of Rav Yeiva Sava, the general rule is: Zeir Anpin is called “You”; Atika Kadisha, which is concealed, is called “He.” This is fitting. Here, however, we call the place where a beginning is found “You.” Although it is concealed, a beginning proceeds from it, and it is called “Father,” the father of the fathers. This Father emerges from Atika Kadisha, as it is written: “Wisdom is found from ayin,” and therefore it is not known.”

h: Oral Torah Flowing Into the Heart

p: וְתֵיבַת לֵאמֹר מְרַמֵּז עַל חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין, נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— The word leimor, “saying,” alludes to the field of apples, the souls of Israel,
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַשְׁפִּיעַ בָּהֶם הַטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא,
— within whom the Holy One, blessed be He, causes the dew of Atika to flow.
וְזֶהוּ לֵאמֹר, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נֶאֱמַר זֶה בִּלְבָבוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
— This is “saying”: that it should be uttered within the hearts of Israel.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ עַל פָּסוּק תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי,
— As we explained on “My utterance shall flow like dew,”
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁנּוֹזֶלֶת מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא,
— it alludes to the Oral Torah flowing from the dew of Atika.
וַאֲמִירָה הוּא בַּחֲשַׁאי וּבַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אָמַרְתִּי אֲנִי בְּלִבִּי, וַיֹּאמֶר הָמָן בְּלִבּוֹ,
— Utterance is quiet and inward, as it says, “I said in my heart,” and “Haman said in his heart”
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ רלד ב).
— (as taught in the holy Zohar on this portion, 234b).
וְכֵן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נוֹזֵל גַּם כֵּן בַּלֵּב וּבִלְחִישׁוּ,
— The Oral Torah likewise flows into the heart in a whisper,
שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּאִלּוּ הַחֲכָמִים מְחַדְּשִׁים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר י).
— appearing as though the sages themselves originate it (as explained in discourse 10).
וְאוֹת וָא״ו שֶׁבְּתֵיבַת לֵאמוֹר מְרַמֵּז עַל זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין,
— The letter vav in leimor alludes to Zeir Anpin,
דְּו׳ שֶׁבַּשֵּׁם הוּא זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין כַּיָּדוּעַ, וּמְרַמֵּז עַל ו׳ הַמִּדּוֹת, הַו׳ קְצָווֹת.
— for the vav of the Name is Zeir Anpin, as is known, and alludes to the six attributes, the six extremities.
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּקְרָא) דְּאוֹת ו׳ אִיקְרֵי אוֹת אֱמֶת וְאוֹת חַיִּים,
— The holy Zohar, at the beginning of Vayikra, teaches that vav is called the letter of truth and the letter of life,
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם בְּלֹא הֶפְסֵק לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד.
— alluding to eternal life, unbroken forever.
וְזֶה שֶׁבֵּירַךְ אֶת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא יִהְיֶה מְקוֹר הַשְׁפָּעַת הַבְּרָכוֹת,
— This is why he blessed Joseph to become the source of the flow of blessings,
כִּדְאִיתָא (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תּוֹלְדוֹת) דְּמוּסַף שַׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא רִיבּוּי הַקְּדוּשָּׁה דְּשַׁבָּת, בְּרָזָא דְּיוֹסֵף,
— as Zohar Chadash, Toldot, teaches: Shabbat Musaf, the increase of Shabbat’s holiness, belongs to the mystery of Joseph.
כִּי בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף קְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית, וְהוּא רָזָא דְּשַׁבָּת.
— Joseph’s aspect is the holiness of the covenant, which is the mystery of Shabbat.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב׳ קלה ב),
— This is what the holy Zohar says (II, 135b):
וּבְגִין דְּאִיהוּ מְקוֹרָא בְּרָזָא דְּאָת קַייָּמָא קָרִינָן לֵיהּ הַמְּבוֹרָךְ,
— Because it is the source, in the mystery of the sign of the covenant, we call it “the blessed.”
אִיהוּ מַבּוּעָא דְּבֵירָא וְכוּלֵי, וְכֵיוָן דְּמָטָאן הָתָם כֻּלְּהוּ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד.
— It is the spring of the well, and so forth; once they all reach there, they endure forever.
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁבֵּרְכָם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא לֵאמוֹר שֶׁהוּא הַשְׁפָּעַת הַבְּרָכוֹת מֵהַמָּקוֹר,
— By blessing them “on that day, saying,” which is the influx of blessings from their source,
עַל כֵּן אָמַר בְּךָ יְבָרֵךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— he therefore said, “Through you Israel shall bless.”
שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה שֶׁל הַמְשָׁכַת הַבְּרָכוֹת הוּא חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק.
— For this drawing of blessings is the portion of Joseph the Righteous.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 234b: ““He said”—what is meant by “he said”? We have explained it, as in “You will say in your heart”: speech in a whisper. “Gather yourselves”: should it not say “Gather,” as in “Gather My faithful ones to Me”? Rather, we know that “Gather yourselves” comes from the place above: gather yourselves in a complete bond, in a single unity. “I will tell you”—what does “I will tell” mean? It is a mystery of wisdom. Rabbi Yosei asked Rabbi Shimon: We learned that “I will tell,” “he told,” “they will tell,” and similar forms are a mystery of wisdom. Why does this expression embody a mystery of wisdom? He answered: Because the letters gimel and dalet come together without separation. This is the mystery of wisdom: a word that comes in completeness through the mystery of the letters is such when they are in wisdom. But dalet without gimel is not complete, nor is gimel without dalet. They are bound to one another without separation; whoever separates them brings death upon himself, and this is the mystery of Adam’s sin. Therefore this expression is a mystery of wisdom. Although a yod sometimes stands between gimel and dalet, it causes no separation: everything is a single bond. Thus the expression is certainly precise. “I will tell you”—a mystery of wisdom: he wished to reveal the final outcome of all Israel’s deeds.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 2a: ““Ask for yourself a sign”—literally a letter, for all of them acted through the mystery of the letters. Likewise, what is written concerning Rahab? “Give me a true sign.” This is the letter vav, which is called the letter of truth. Should you say that the other letters are not true? They are, but this letter is called the letter of truth.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Toldot, Sitrei Torah §§3–7: “Come and see: The Holy One, blessed be He, created seven supernal days in the world, and upon them He planted and built worlds. Thus it is written: “For six days Hashem made,” rather than “in six days.” Corresponding to those seven supernal days, He created seven truly righteous people on earth to uphold and illuminate them, each corresponding to his day. He planted each in the generation fitting for him. These are the fathers of the world: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, and David. They are called mountains, the ancient mountains, for they depend upon those seven supernal days: six days of Creation, and a seventh standing before them, as it says, “The house of David will be like God, like the angel of Hashem before them.” Although it is seventh, it is fourth among the days, and Joseph is seventh. But when it is included in Joseph, and he gives it an added delight from the King’s house, it too is called seventh. All of them hold fast to the Shekhinah in the mystery of seven, for the Shekhinah is called Bat-Sheva: a daughter of the supernal Mother, who includes the seven degrees with her. She is the degree of Tzedek, the tenth of the sefirot by which the Holy One, blessed be He, is called.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: The passage locates the added delight of Shabbat in its inclusion within Joseph. Rav Tzadok applies this “addition” to Shabbat Musaf.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 135b: ““Bless et Hashem”—et is precise, as we have said: this is Shabbat at the entrance of Shabbat. “Blessed is Hashem, the blessed One”—this is the drawing forth of blessings from the source of life, the place from which all watering issues to irrigate everything. Because it is the source, in the mystery of the sign of the covenant, we call it “the blessed One.” It is the spring of the well. Once they reach there, the well is certainly filled, and its waters never cease.”
